summary: The main article describes a nickel-catalyzed transamidation of secondary aliphatic amides using a Boc-activation strategy. It includes one optimization table, three scope figures (amide substrate, N-substituent, and amine nucleophile), and two figures detailing competition studies and enantioenriched substrate applications.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: Challenges associated with secondary amide transamidation and the two step-approach to realize this challenging synthetic transformation.
items.description: Illustrates the kinetic and thermodynamic barriers of transamidation and the proposed solution using Boc-activation and Ni-catalysis.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of the reaction conditions
items.description: Lists the screening of ligands, bases, and concentrations to optimize the yield of the transamidation product 9.

items.heading: Fig. 2
items.caption: Variation of the amide substrate. Yields shown re fl ect the average of two isolation experiments.
items.description: Shows the scope of the reaction with respect to different aliphatic amide partners, including sterically hindered and heterocyclic examples.

items.heading: Fig. 3
items.caption: Scope of the amide substrate N -substituent. Yields shown re fl ect the average of two isolation experiments.
items.description: Demonstrates that various N-alkyl groups on the amide substrate are tolerated in the transamidation process.

items.heading: Fig. 4
items.caption: Scope of the amine nucleophile. Yields shown re fl ect the average of two isolation experiments. a Yield determined by 1 H NMR analysis using 1,3,5-trimethoxybenzene as an internal standard.
items.description: Explores the range of amine nucleophiles, including primary, secondary, and aniline derivatives, that can participate in the reaction.

items.heading: Fig. 5
items.caption: A series of amine competition experiments. Yields determined by 1 H NMR analysis using hexamethylbenzene as an internal standard.
items.description: Presents competition studies between different amines to establish selectivity patterns based on sterics and nucleophilicity.

items.heading: Fig. 6
items.caption: Transamidation of enantioenriched amide substrate 38 on gram-scale and transamidation of enantioenriched N -Boc proline substrate 40 using a modi fi ed protocol.
items.description: Highlights the synthetic utility of the method for gram-scale reactions and its compatibility with epimerizable stereocenters.
